question: The substance which doctors use as plaster for supporting fractured bones in the right position is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**CaSO4⋅1/2H2O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The substance doctors use as plaster for supporting fractured bones is **Plaster of Paris**.

 
• **Plaster of Paris Composition:** Plaster of Paris is a type of gypsum plaster derived from calcium sulfate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O).
 
• **Production Process:** It is produced by heating gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O) to a specific temperature, typically around 120-140 degrees Celsius.
 
• **Chemical Reaction:** This heating process removes some of the water molecules from the gypsum, converting it to the hemihydrate form.
 
• **Setting Reaction:** When Plaster of Paris is mixed with water, it rehydrates to form calcium sulfate dihydrate, the original gypsum.
 
• **Crystallization:** This rehydration process leads to the formation of interlocking crystals, which give the plaster its hardness and rigidity.
 
• **Application in Medicine:** Doctors use Plaster of Paris to create casts and splints for immobilizing fractured bones, allowing them to heal properly in the correct alignment.
 
• **Support and Immobilization:** The rigid cast provides support to the injured limb, preventing movement and reducing pain.
 
• **Bone Healing:** Immobilization is essential for proper bone healing, as it allows the bone fragments to knit together and mend.
 
• **Preparation of Casts:** To create a cast, Plaster of Paris powder is mixed with water to form a paste.
 
• **Bandaging:** This paste is then applied to bandages (gauze or stockinette) which are wrapped around the injured limb.
 
• **Setting Time:** The plaster sets relatively quickly, typically within a few minutes, hardening into a solid cast.
 
• **Customization:** The casts can be molded and shaped to fit the specific contours of the injured limb, providing a snug and supportive fit.
 
• **Lightweight and Durable:** Once set, the cast is relatively lightweight yet strong and durable, providing adequate support for the healing bone.
 
• **X-ray Permeability:** Plaster of Paris is permeable to X-rays, allowing doctors to monitor the healing progress of the fracture without removing the cast.
 
• **Removal:** When the bone has healed sufficiently, the cast can be removed, usually with the help of a cast saw.
 
• **Other Uses:** Besides medical applications, Plaster of Paris is also used in construction, art, and decorative purposes.
 
• **Safety Considerations:** While generally safe, some individuals may experience skin irritation or allergic reactions to Plaster of Paris.
